definition: An unhealthy belief in your own importance, which he calls the enemy inside the work.
example: Wherever you are, your worst enemy already lives inside you: your ego.

definition: A grounded estimate of yourself. He wants it rock-hard, not soft or performed.
example: What replaces ego is humility, yes — but rock-hard humility and confidence.

definition: Earned trust in your ability, which he separates from swagger that was only borrowed.
example: Whereas ego is artificial, this type of confidence can hold weight.

definition: Made up rather than earned. His word for the confidence ego pretends to have.
example: Whereas ego is artificial, this type of confidence can hold weight.

definition: Genuinely worthy of respect, as distinct from merely looking successful.
example: Impressing people is utterly different from being truly impressive.

definition: Real command of a subject, which a title can imitate without possessing.
example: Having authority is not the same as being an authority.

definition: Work you clear so someone else can do their best, which later opens a path for you.
example: Find canvases for other people to paint on.

definition: Heated wanting that, in his warning, often covers a lack of discipline.
example: Passion typically masks a weakness.

definition: A soft spot that loud passion can hide from the person who has it.
example: Passion typically masks a weakness.

definition: Trained self-command, the replacement he offers for the temptations of ego.
example: Replace the temptations of ego with humility and discipline when you experience success.

definition: A steady inner quiet that lets you act without frenzy while the world spins.
example: Stillness is what aims the archer's arrow. It inspires new ideas.

definition: Wild, hurried agitation. Stillness, in his definition, is acting without it.
example: To be steady while the world spins around you. To act without frenzy.

definition: A state of quiet, outside and in, that can be called up on purpose.
example: To possess quietude — exterior and interior — on command.

definition: The ability to stay unshaken. One of the old names he gathers under stillness.
example: You would have heard equally emphatic calls for this imperturbability, unruffledness, and tranquility.

definition: Settled calm, the condition the old schools treated as a high good.
example: You would have heard equally emphatic calls for this imperturbability, unruffledness, and tranquility.

definition: The state of not being thrown off by noise, threat, or praise.
example: You would have heard equally emphatic calls for this imperturbability, unruffledness, and tranquility.

definition: What blocks the path, and in his thesis becomes the path.
example: The obstacle in the path becomes the path.

definition: A chance to improve your condition that sits inside the difficulty.
example: Within every obstacle is an opportunity to improve our condition.

definition: Strength of mind that keeps a failure from wrecking you.
example: Cultivate strength and fortitude so that when fate turns against you, you're not wrecked by failure.

definition: Able to recover. The stance he wants once failure arrives.
example: The aim is to be humble in aspiration, gracious in success, and resilient in failure.

definition: An inflated sense of superiority, the everyday face of the ego he warns against.
example: Arrogance and self-centered ambition are the casual definition of ego he uses.

definition: Careful, sustained effort. One of the traits he says actually gets people there.
example: What separated them was not talent or confidence, but humility, diligence, and self-awareness.
